speaker: Unknown
en: Hi, listeners.
zh: 听众们，大家好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome back to No Priors.
zh: 欢迎回到 No Priors。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, I'm here with Stefano Erman, who is a longtime Stanford professor and now co-founder and CEO of Inception.
zh: 今天我做客的嘉宾是 Stefano Erman，他是斯坦福大学的资深教授，现在也是 Inception 的联合创始人兼 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: Stefano has an extraordinarily broad body of work around generative modeling, but is especially well-known as one of the fathers of diffusion.
zh: Stefano 在生成式建模领域有着极其广泛的研究成果，但他最为人熟知的身份是扩散模型的奠基人之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: We talk about his company, challenging the large labs, and why speed and efficiency are going to be the name of the game in AI over the next few years.
zh: 我们会聊到他的公司、对大型实验室的挑战，以及为什么在未来几年里，速度和效率将成为 AI 领域的制胜关键。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome, Stefano.
zh: 欢迎，Stefano。

speaker: Unknown
en: Stefano, thanks so much for being here.
zh: Stefano，非常感谢你能来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great to be here.
zh: 很高兴来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would love for us to just start with a little bit of your research background and how you ended up starting your company.
zh: 我很想先从你的研究背景聊起，以及你是怎么最终创立了自己的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: For sure, yeah.
zh: 当然，好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been doing research in generative models for like basically my entire career.
zh: 基本上我的整个职业生涯都在做生成式模型方面的研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: I started at Stanford in 2014 as an assistant professor.
zh: 我于 2014 年以助理教授的身份加入斯坦福。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was working on building generative models.
zh: 当时我在做构建生成式模型的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Back then, the research area was not particularly hot.
zh: 那个时候，这个研究领域并不算特别热门。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, the models were not quite working well.
zh: 你知道，那时的模型效果并不太好。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were still like building little generative models over MNIST.
zh: 我们还在构建针对 MNIST 的小型生成式模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was like a big success if you could generate these grainy images of digits.
zh: 如果你能生成这些模糊的数字图像，那就算是一项巨大的成功了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, it was even hard to publish papers back then on that topic.
zh: 而且，你知道，那时候在这个话题上发表 论文都很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you had to kind of like justify
zh: 你还不得不某种程度上去论证，

speaker: Unknown
en: Training a generative model as a way to learn features from unlabeled data that then could maybe help you do better at supervised learning, because that was the thing that everybody cared about.
zh: 训练生成式模型是一种从无标注数据中学习特征的方式，而这些特征之后也许能帮助你在监督学习上做得更好，因为那才是当时所有人关心的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then, you know, things took over, of course.
zh: 但后来，你知道，情况就逆转了，当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it was like I was at the right place at the right time, working on the right thing.
zh: 所以就像是我恰好在正确的时间、正确的地点，做着正确的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I've been doing research in that space since the beginning, basically.
zh: 所以从最开始，我就一直在那个领域做研究，基本上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Did you have like a, besides curiosity in the area, a personal hope for what the models would do back in 2014 and 15?
zh: 除了对这个领域的好奇心之外，你在 2014、15 年的时候，对这些模型能做到什么，有没有一种个人的期望？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, I always felt like that was going to be the, that was the right way to think about kind of like learning from unlabeled data, that like building a generative model is really the right way to make sure you understand the structure in the data.
zh: 是的，我的意思是，我一直觉得那就是……那就是思考如何从无标注数据中学习的正确方式，也就是说，构建一个生成式模型，才是真正能确保你理解数据中结构的正确方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was kind of like the way I was getting at.
zh: 那大概就是我当时的切入点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was not even dreaming about the kind of capabilities that these LLMs that we have today could do that.
zh: 我当时甚至做梦都没想到，我们今天拥有的这些 LLM 能做到的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I was thinking more from, I think, world models perspective.
zh: 但我想我当时更多是从，我认为，世界模型的角度来思考的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I was working a lot on images and so thinking about, okay, like...
zh: 比如，我当时在图像上做了很多工作，所以会想，好，比如……

speaker: Unknown
en: I have a world model.
zh: 我有一个世界模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can imagine what's going to happen if I were to stand up and walk out the door.
zh: 我能想象如果我站起来走出这扇门会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I can kind of like picture that in my mind.
zh: 比如我可以在脑海里大致描绘出那个画面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's important to make decisions and kind of like model predictive control when having this kind of model of the world requires some generative capabilities.
zh: 而这对于做决策很重要，有点像模型预测控制，拥有这种关于世界的模型需要一些生成能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I always felt like, okay, that's the right direction to work on.
zh: 所以我一直觉得，好，那是值得研究的正确方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: I felt like this is going to be very hard as a problem.
zh: 我当时觉得这会是一个非常难的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, it's going to keep me busy for my whole career.
zh: 就像是，它会让我忙上整整一辈子的职业生涯。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's a good problem to work on.
zh: 所以这是一个值得研究的好问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then of course I was very wrong and things.
zh: 然后当然我错得很离谱，事情……

speaker: Unknown
en: It evolved much faster than I was expecting.
zh: 它的演进比我预期的要快得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think that's kind of universally true though.
zh: 是的，我觉得这在某种程度上是普遍成立的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sort of walk me through the state of your research and how that led you to start the company.
zh: 那能带我们了解一下你研究的进程，以及它是如何引导你创立公司的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so I was working on generative models of images, initially working on autoregressive models, which were very slow and kind of like very blurry and then VAEs and then GANs took over.
zh: 是的，我最初在做图像的生成式模型，先是从自回归模型做起，它们非常慢，而且生成结果很模糊，然后是 VAE，接着 GAN 成了主流。

speaker: Unknown
en: And back then we were very unhappy with the state of generative models for images, like the GANs were
zh: 那时候我们对图像生成式模型的现状非常不满意，比如当时的 GAN……

speaker: Unknown
en: They worked, but they were very unstable to train, very hard to reproduce results.
zh: 它们能工作，但训练起来非常不稳定，结果非常难以复现。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we were trying to say, is there a way to build something that is as good as a GAN, but it's more principled?
zh: 所以我们当时想问，有没有办法构建一个和 GAN 一样好，但更有原则性的东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we started working on score-based, the generative models, which are basically what eventually became diffusion models back in 2019 with my PhD student Yang Song.
zh: 于是我们开始研究基于分数的生成式模型，这基本上就是后来在 2019 年与我的博士生 Yang Song 一起最终演变成扩散模型的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we kind of like came up with this idea of let's train a neural network to denoise images.
zh: 于是我们大致想出了这个点子：训练一个神经网络来给图像去噪。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you can denoise an image, then you really are understanding enough about the structure of the image that it should be possible to build a generative procedure based on these denoisers.
zh: 如果你能给一张图像去噪，那说明你对图像的结构已经有了足够深入的理解，那么基于这些去噪器构建一个生成过程应该是可行的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that basically became the underlying technology of modern diffusion models, where instead of generating images left to right one pixel at a time, you start from pure noise, and then you gradually refine the object until you get a clean picture at the end.
zh: 而这基本上就成了现代扩散模型的底层技术：不是从左到右一个像素一个像素地生成图像，而是从纯噪声开始，然后逐渐 refine 这个对象，直到最后得到一张干净的图像。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that started back in 2019 in my lab, and then it kind of like took over the space.
zh: 这始于 2019 年我的实验室，然后它就逐渐占领了整个领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even today, the best models for image generation, video generation, music to some extent, a lot of the protein stuff, they are based on diffusion.
zh: 甚至在今天,最好的图像生成、视频生成、某种程度上音乐生成,还有大量蛋白质方面的工作,都是基于 diffusion 的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so my group has worked a lot on various kinds of diffusion models, technique for accelerating them to generate samples very quickly.
zh: 所以我的团队在各种各样的 diffusion 模型上做了很多工作,研究加速它们、快速生成样本的技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: To improve the quality of these models.
zh: 以提升这些模型的质量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so since we were able to get them to work on images, I started thinking about how do we get diffusion models to work on text or code generation and the discrete objects?
zh: 既然我们能让 diffusion 在图像上奏效,我开始思考如何让 diffusion 模型用在文本或代码生成这些离散对象上?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, is there a way to move beyond autoregressive models to something that it's more parallel, more with built-in error correction?
zh: 比如,有没有办法超越自回归模型,走向更并行、内置纠错能力的东西?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I've been doing a bunch of research at Stanford on getting diffusion models to work on text and code generation.
zh: 所以我在 Stanford 做了很多研究,让 diffusion 模型用于文本和代码生成。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had a breakthrough in 2024.
zh: 我们在 2024 年取得了突破。

speaker: Unknown
en: We published a paper basically showing that for the first time it was possible to match the quality of an autoregressive model at the GPT-2 scale.
zh: 我们发表了一篇论文,基本证明了首次可以在 GPT-2 规模上匹配自回归模型的质量。

speaker: Unknown
en: So less than a billion parameters, still fairly academic.
zh: 也就是不到十亿参数,仍然相当学术化。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we were able to train basically still a transformer model as a diffusion model on the same data.
zh: 但我们基本上能用仍然是 transformer 的模型、以 diffusion 模型的方式、在同样的数据上训练。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were able to match the quality, like the same perplexity, and you were fitting the data just as well as an autoregressive model with the same number of parameters.
zh: 我们能够匹配质量,比如同样的困惑度,而且在参数数量相同的情况下,对数据的拟合程度和自回归模型一样好。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the diffusion model was significantly faster.
zh: 但 diffusion 模型明显更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because it's diffusion, because you're outputting many tokens at the same time, we were able to generate text like 10x faster compared to the autoregressive model.
zh: 因为它是 diffusion,因为你同时输出很多 token,我们能够比自回归模型快大约 10 倍地生成文本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that felt very, very exciting.
zh: 所以这让人感觉非常、非常令人兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I really wanted to see what happens if you scale up, if you train bigger models.
zh: 我非常想知道如果扩大规模、训练更大的模型会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I started Inception, a company to basically scale up the technology and then try to build commercial scale diffusion-based language models.
zh: 于是我创办了 Inception,这家公司基本上就是把这项技术扩大规模,然后尝试构建商业规模的基于 diffusion 的语言模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone has now seen the outputs of diffusion models in particular images.
zh: 现在每个人都见过 diffusion 模型的输出,尤其是图像。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I would argue that it's like increasingly a dominant form of like generated short form video from diffusion models is like a dominant form of entertainment in other parts of the world.
zh: 我想说,从 diffusion 模型生成的短视频正日益成为一种主导形式,在世界其他地方,它已经成为一种主要的娱乐形式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it will likely become so here.
zh: 而且它很可能在这里也会变成这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of unbelievable, at least to me, even having followed the field for the last decade plus, the quality that is possible today.
zh: 有点难以置信,至少对我来说是这样,即使我已经追踪这个领域十多年了,今天所能达到的质量依然令人惊叹。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that is kind of obvious, right?
zh: 所以我觉得这一点是显而易见的,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's such a big use case in images and video generation that folks are even creating hardware to support better performance here.
zh: 而且图像和视频生成的用例如此之大,以至于人们甚至在为支持这方面更好的性能而专门制造硬件。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not intuitive that would work for other fields or that, you know, this is a interesting competitive direction to the current, you know, full transformer focus like AGI labs.
zh: 但它能否适用于其他领域并不直观,或者说,这是对当前、你知道的,专注于 transformer 的 AGI 实验室的一个有趣的竞争方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you offer some intuition on that?
zh: 你能就此提供一些直觉上的解释吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so it's a very interesting kind of like state of the world right now from a researcher perspective, because like there is like two main paradigms, two ways of building generative models.
zh: 好的,从研究者的角度看,这是一个非常有趣的当前世界状态,因为主要有两种范式、两种构建生成模型的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is autoregressive, where you kind of like have a model that predicts the next token or the next pixel, and then you generate left to right one token at a time.
zh: 一种是自回归,你有一个模型预测下一个 token 或下一个像素,然后从左到右一次生成一个 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's diffusion, which is a course to find generation, kind of like iterative denoising kind of generation.
zh: 另一种是 diffusion,这是一种从粗到精的生成,有点像迭代去噪式的生成。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as you said, like we have continuous modalities where diffusion dominate,
zh: 正如你所说,在连续模态上 diffusion 占主导地位,

speaker: Unknown
en: There is discrete modalities, text and code, where primarily all the big labs are betting on the same architecture, autoregressive models.
zh: 而存在离散模态,文本和代码,所有大实验室基本上都在押注同一个架构——自回归模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as we move towards more and more multimodal models, there is this idea that maybe we'll have a model that can handle all modalities and we'll know everything about the world.
zh: 随着我们走向越来越多的多模态模型,有这样一种想法:也许我们会拥有一个能处理所有模态、并且了解世界一切的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: What architecture would that be?
zh: 那会是什么样的架构?

speaker: Unknown
en: Will it be an autoregressive model?
zh: 会是自回归模型吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Will it be a diffusion model?
zh: 会是 diffusion 模型吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody knows.
zh: 没人知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the jury's still out there.
zh: 我认为还没有定论。

speaker: Unknown
en: At inception, we're betting on diffusion models because we believe that what matters eventually will be inference time scaling.
zh: 在 Inception,我们押注 diffusion 模型,因为我们相信最终重要的是推理时扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are fundamental reasons for why diffusion models are better than autoregressive models at inference time.
zh: 而且,有一些根本性的原因说明为什么 diffusion 模型在推理时优于自回归模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So even if you think about the story of autoregressive models,
zh: 即便你回想一下自回归模型的故事,

speaker: Unknown
en: There was an inflection point in 2017 when people switched from RNNs to Transformers, right?
zh: 2017 年有一个转折点,人们从 RNN 转向了 Transformer,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And what was that?
zh: 那是怎么回事?

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem was that RNNs had to essentially process tokens sequentially, one at a time.
zh: 问题是 RNN 本质上必须按顺序逐个处理 token,一次一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And training was very slow.
zh: 训练非常慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so people came up with this idea of let's have an architecture that allows you to process many tokens at the same time in parallel.
zh: 于是人们提出了这个想法:让我们设计一种架构,允许你同时并行处理很多 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was a transformer.
zh: 那就是 Transformer。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was the thing that scaled better for training and that enabled a lot of the successes behind LLAMs.
zh: 那是在训练上扩展性更好的东西,并促成了 LLAM 背后的许多成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you think about inference, not training, inference generation, autoregressive models are still sequential.
zh: 但如果你想到推理,而不是训练,推理生成,自回归模型仍然是顺序的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The computation is one left to right, one token at a time.
zh: 计算是从左到右的,一次一个 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: You cannot generate the 10th token until you've generated everything that comes before it.
zh: 在生成它之前所有内容之前,你无法生成第 10 个 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: That kind of workload does not map well to GPUs.
zh: 这种工作负载并不能很好地映射到 GPU 上。

speaker: Unknown
en: That kind of workload is extremely memory bound.
zh: 这种工作负载是极其受内存限制的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're spending most of your time moving around weights across the memory hierarchy and you're doing very little arithmetic.
zh: 你把大部分时间花在内存层次结构之间搬运权重上，而你做的算术运算非常少。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's a fundamental problem of autoregressive models.
zh: 而这是自回归模型的一个根本问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what's the equivalent if you think RNNs, Transformers?
zh: 那么如果你想想 RNN、Transformer,对应的东西是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Autoregressive models, the equivalent at inference time is a diffusion model.
zh: 自回归模型，在推理时对应的就是扩散模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because a diffusion model is built to have at inference time a workload where you process many tokens at the same time.
zh: 因为扩散模型生来就是让推理时的工作负载可以同时处理很多 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the workload that we have at inference time in a diffusion model
zh: 所以我们在扩散模型推理时拥有的工作负载

speaker: Unknown
en: It's basically very, very similar to the workload you have for training, where you are processing many tokens at the same time in parallel.
zh: 基本上和训练时的工作负载非常非常相似，都是同时并行处理很多 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's built to essentially have an inference workload that maps really, really well to map modes, the kind of things GPUs do really, really well.
zh: 所以它生来就有一种推理工作负载，能非常非常好地映射到那种 GPU 真正真正擅长做的事情上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we bet on trying to build the architecture and trying to build the kind of models that will scale best at inference time.
zh: 所以我们押注于尝试构建那种在推理时扩展性最好的架构和模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because, you know, economics are dominated by, you know, the kind of intelligence per watt, the intelligence per dollar that you're able to get from the models.
zh: 因为，你知道，经济性主要取决于你从模型中能获得的每瓦特智能、每美元智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about a lot of the advances with reasoning models, a lot of it is scaling test and compute, right?
zh: 如果想想推理模型的很多进展，很多都是扩展测试时计算，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so being able to scale better along that axis will also matter.
zh: 所以能在这个轴上扩展得更好也会很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even if you think about RL post-training, a lot of the bottleneck is generating rollouts, like letting the model explore,
zh: 甚至想想 RL 后训练，很多瓶颈在于生成 rollout,比如让模型去探索，

speaker: Unknown
en: And then scoring the trajectories and then improving the model based on the kind of things it finds.
zh: 然后给轨迹打分，再根据模型发现的东西来改进模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so inference is, again, a key bottleneck for RL post-training.
zh: 所以推理又是 RL 后训练的一个关键瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you have a model that scales better at inference time, then automatically you're going to get better scaling during RL post-training.
zh: 所以如果你有一个推理时扩展性更好的模型，那么你在 RL 后训练时自然会获得更好的扩展性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's why we decided to bet on a diffusion-based LLM because it's inherently more parallel.
zh: 所以这就是为什么我们决定押注基于扩散的 LLM,因为它天生更具并行性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the better lesson is that the more parallel solution is the one that is eventually going to win.
zh: 更好的教训是，更具并行性的方案就是最终会胜出的那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you think about applicability or what experiments did you run in terms of cracking the nut on discrete versus continuous modalities?
zh: 你如何看待适用性，或者你做了哪些实验来攻克离散与连续模态这个难题？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I think people have also shaped the existing, you know, dominant paradigm through
zh: 因为我觉得人们也通过
